title: Demonstrations over living costs in Lille and Bordeaux

tea.why: Protesters demonstrated over rising living costs and public services.
tea.want: No specific demands were stated in the sources.
tea.changed: Oct 22: Stolen iPhones from targeted stores displayed security warnings and tracking alerts.

summary: On October 17, 2026, demonstrations took place in French cities including Lille and Bordeaux, driven by concerns over rising living costs and public services. During the unrest, businesses including the Apple Store on Rue Faidherbe in Lille and the Apple Sainte-Catherine location in Bordeaux were targeted by looters. Videos circulated online showed individuals taking merchandise from the stores. Subsequently, reports emerged that stolen iPhones displayed security warnings indicating the devices were disabled, geolocated, and that authorities would be notified. Authorities faced pressure to address the widespread disruption and investigate incidents of theft and property damage.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Demonstrations and looting occurred at retail locations in Lille and Bordeaux amid nationwide unrest.
Reports indicated stolen iPhones from the targeted stores displayed security warnings and tracking alerts.
